screening_decisions.reason: The intervention was administered intravenously (single 200 mg iv dose), but the selection criteria require orally administered tricyclic drugs.
The intervention is fluoxetine (an SSRI), not a tricyclic antidepressant.
Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial comparing oral nortriptyline (a tricyclic) with placebo in depressed adolescents aged 12–17 years.
This is a qualitative narrative review, not a randomised controlled trial.
Double-blind pilot RCT comparing oral imipramine (a tricyclic) with placebo in depressed children; plasma levels reported are consistent with oral dosing.
Double-blind crossover RCT comparing oral amitriptyline (a tricyclic) with placebo in children aged 9–12 years with major depressive disorder.
Review of newer generation antidepressants (SSRIs), not tricyclics, and not a primary RCT of a tricyclic versus placebo.
RCT comparing oral imipramine plus CBT with placebo plus CBT in school-refusing adolescents with comorbid major depressive disorder; meets population and intervention criteria.
Double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT comparing oral imipramine with placebo in prepubertal children with major depressive disorder.
Three-arm RCT that includes a direct comparison of oral imipramine (a tricyclic) versus placebo in depressed adolescents, fulfilling the selection criteria.
Narrative review discussing mechanisms of antidepressants, not a randomised controlled trial.
Review of SSRI overdose safety data; not an RCT of tricyclics versus placebo for depression in young people.
Methodological paper on meta-analysis statistics; not a clinical trial.
Case series/review of amitriptyline poisoning and intoxication, not an efficacy RCT.

Appears to be a secondary analysis or commentary on predictors of treatment response; the abstract does not specify that the drug was a tricyclic antidepressant and does not clearly describe a primary RCT of tricyclic versus placebo.
RCT comparing oral desipramine (a tricyclic) with placebo in adolescents aged 13–18 years with major depression.
Narrative review and commentary on psychopharmacology, not a primary randomised controlled trial.

Includes a double-blind, placebo-controlled study with an imipramine arm versus placebo in children/adolescents with school refusal; depression rating scales were used as outcomes. Although the primary diagnosis is school refusal, the conservative approach is to include this for full-text review.
Case series of accidental TCA ingestions evaluated by a poison control center; not an efficacy RCT.
Randomised, double-blind, parallel-design, placebo-controlled trial of oral amitriptyline in adolescents aged 12–17 years with major depressive disorder.
The abstract does not confirm a placebo comparison group, and the population is described as having school phobia/neurotic disorder rather than clearly depressed people.
Meta-analysis of studies in adults (aged 18–65 years) comparing paroxetine with amitriptyline; does not compare a tricyclic with placebo and does not include children or adolescents.
Observational study examining the relationship between plasma imipramine levels and clinical response; no placebo comparison group is described.
Randomised, controlled trial comparing oral amitriptyline with placebo in adolescents with major depressive disorder.
Secondary analysis focusing on medication compliance, side effects, and blinding; it does not report an efficacy comparison between imipramine and placebo.
